level.title: Intermediate: stories, opinions, work, plans
goals: Tell stories with pretérito and imperfeito
Compare things and argue opinions politely
Handle work talk and make future plans

lessons.title: Stories: pretérito vs imperfeito
lessons.learn: Two pasts! PRETÉRITO = finished actions (CHEGUEI = I arrived). IMPERFEITO = ongoing scenes (FAZIA SOL = it was sunny). Set scenes with imperfeito, fire events with pretérito.

grammar.title: Pretérito vs imperfeito: falei vs falava
grammar.explain: FALEI = I spoke (done). FALAVA = I was speaking/used to speak (ongoing). -AR imperfeito: FALAVA, FALAVA, FALAVA — all the same! Weather, feelings, habits → imperfeito. Single events → pretérito.

examples.en: I was speaking when you arrived.

mistakes: Using pretérito for weather: FAZIA sol, not FEZ sol.
Using imperfeito for arrivals: CHEGUEI, not CHEGAVA.

dialogue.en: It was great. There was music and we danced.

dialogue.r: kee leh-GAH-oo!

lessons.title: Opinions and comparisons
lessons.learn: Compare with MAIS…DO QUE (more…than) and MENOS…DO QUE. Specials: MELHOR (better), PIOR (worse). Opinions: ACHO QUE (I think that), NA MINHA OPINIÃO (in my opinion).

grammar.title: Comparisons: mais… do que, melhor
grammar.explain: MAIS + adjective + DO QUE = more…than: MAIOR DO QUE = bigger than. O MELHOR = the best. MELHOR and PIOR never take MAIS — complete already!

examples.t: É maior do que minha casa.
examples.r: eh mey-OHR doo kee MEEN-yah KAH-zah.
examples.en: It is bigger than my house.

mistakes: Forgetting DO QUE: MAIOR DO QUE, with DO QUE!

lessons.title: Contar uma história: os conectores
lessons.learn: A story in Portuguese hangs on four connectors: quando opens the event, enquanto holds the background, de repente breaks it, and no fim lands it. They are placed at the head of the clause, and the verb follows the tense rule you already know — imperfeito for the scene, pretérito for the event.

grammar.title: Linking a narrative
grammar.pattern: quando + event · enquanto + scene · de repente + event · no fim + result
grammar.explain: Portuguese keeps the scene in the imperfeito and moves it with the pretérito. Connectors do not change that: enquanto eu voltava (scene), de repente começou a chover (event). No fim das contas and afinal close a story with a judgement.

examples.t: Quando eu cheguei, a festa já tinha começado.
examples.r: KWAHN-doo eh-oo sheh-GAY, ah FEHS-tah zhah TEE-nyah koh-meh-SAH-doo.
examples.en: When I arrived, the party had already started.

examples.t: Enquanto eu esperava, li o jornal inteiro.
examples.r: ey(n)-KWAHN-too eh-oo es-peh-RAH-vah, lee oo zhohr-NAH-oo een-TAY-roo.
examples.en: While I was waiting, I read the whole newspaper.

examples.t: No fim das contas, valeu a pena.
examples.r: noo fee(n) dahs KOHN-tahs, vah-LEH-oo ah PEH-nah.
examples.en: In the end, it was worth it.

mistakes.wrong: Enquanto eu esperei, li o jornal.
mistakes.right: Enquanto eu esperava, li o jornal.
mistakes.why: Enquanto frames a scene: imperfeito, not pretérito.
De repente introduces an event: pretérito.

dialogue.t: Conta como foi a viagem.

dialogue.en: When I arrived it was raining hard, so I stayed in the hotel.

dialogue.t: E no dia seguinte?
dialogue.r: ee noo DEE-ah seh-GEEN-jee?
dialogue.en: And the next day?

dialogue.t: De repente o tempo abriu e no fim das contas deu para conhecer tudo.
dialogue.r: jee heh-PEN-jee oo TEH(n)-poo ah-BREE-oo ee noo fee(n) dahs KOHN-tahs deh-oo pah-rah koh-nyeh-SEHR TOO-doo.
dialogue.en: Suddenly the weather cleared and in the end I managed to see everything.

lessons.title: Work and formal you (o senhor)
lessons.learn: At work, VOCÊ fits most people. For extra respect use O SENHOR (sir) / A SENHORA (madam) — with HE/SHE verb forms: O SENHOR FALA inglês? = Do you (formal) speak English?

grammar.title: O SENHOR: formal you uses he-forms
grammar.explain: VOCÊ FALA (standard) vs O SENHOR FALA (extra formal). Same -A ending as HE. A SENHORA for women. Start formal, relax later!
grammar.pattern: o senhor/a senhora + he/she verb form
mistakes: Using TU with a new boss — start with VOCÊ or O SENHOR.
Using FALAS with o senhor — o senhor takes FALA.

dialogue.t: Às dez, no escritório.
dialogue.r: ahsh dehsh, noo shkree-TOH-ryoo.

lessons.title: Wishes: gostaria
lessons.learn: Dream big! GOSTARIA DE (I would like) + verb: GOSTARIA DE VIAJAR = I would like to travel. ESPERO (I hope) opens plans: ESPERO VIAJAR = I hope to travel.

grammar.title: Soft wishes: gostaria de + verb
grammar.explain: GOSTARIA DE = I would like. Add any verb whole: GOSTARIA DE APRENDER = I would like to learn. Note the DE: gostaria DE viajar!
mistakes: Forgetting DE: GOSTARIA DE viajar, with DE!
Changing the verb after GOSTARIA: verb stays whole.

lessons.title: Reunião: concordar, discordar e propor
lessons.learn: A Brazilian meeting disagrees in two steps: first the other position is named (entendo o seu ponto), then the disagreement arrives with a hedge (não sei se concordo, tenho uma ressalva). A proposal is put with que tal or podemos: que tal começarmos pela pauta? The proposal form decides who has to answer.

grammar.title: Disagreeing and proposing
grammar.pattern: entendo o ponto, mas … · tenho uma ressalva · que tal + infinitive
grammar.explain: Direct disagreement is softened by naming what you accept first. Tenho uma ressalva announces a partial objection without rejecting the plan. Que tal and podemos both propose; podemos commits the group more, que tal leaves the decision open.

examples.t: Entendo o ponto, mas tenho uma ressalva sobre o prazo.
examples.r: en-TEN-doo oo POHN-too, mahs teh-nyoo OO-mah heh-SAH-oo-vah SOH-bree oo PRAH-zoo.
examples.en: I see the point, but I have a reservation about the deadline.
How about we start with the agenda?

examples.t: Podemos fechar um acordo até sexta.
examples.r: poh-DEH-moos feh-SHAHR oo(n) ah-KOHR-doo ah-TEH SEHS-tah.
examples.en: We can close an agreement by Friday.

mistakes.wrong: Não sei se eu não concordo.
mistakes.why: The double negative contradicts the hedge.
Que tal takes the personal infinitive quando the subject is we.

lessons.title: Future simple: viajarei
lessons.learn: The real future: VIAJAR → VIAJAREI (I will travel), VIAJARÁ (you/he/she will). Just add -EI/-Á to the whole infinitive — works for -AR, -ER, -IR!

grammar.title: Future: infinitive + ei/á
grammar.explain: Keep the infinitive, add -EI (eu), -Á (você/ele/ela): VIAJAREI, FALARÁ, COMERÁ. One pattern for every verb!
mistakes: Cutting the verb: VIAJAREI keeps -AR + EI.

lessons.title: Media and O/A (it)
lessons.learn: Replace things with O (him/it-m) and A (her/it-f): VEJO O FILME → EU O VEJO (I see it). In Brazil O/A jump BEFORE the verb. News words: NOTÍCIAS, PROGRAMA, FILME.

grammar.title: O/A: it jumps before the verb
grammar.explain: Vejo o filme → EU O VEJO (I see it). Vejo a série → EU A VEJO. O = masculine IT, A = feminine IT. Brazil style: always before!

lessons.title: Relatar o que alguém disse
lessons.learn: When you repeat what someone said, the tense moves back: ela disse que ia chegar tarde, ele falou que tinha visto o relatório. A yes/no question becomes se: perguntou se dava tempo. The reporting verb keeps its own tense, and that is what tells the listener when the original conversation happened.

grammar.title: Reported speech
grammar.pattern: ela disse que ia chegar · ele falou que tinha visto · perguntou se dava
grammar.explain: The tenses step back one: vai → ia, viu → tinha visto, dá → dava. The person shifts to the third person (eu vou → ela disse que ia). For a question, use perguntou se for yes/no and perguntou quando/onde for an information question.

examples.t: Ela disse que ia chegar tarde, mas chegou cedo.
examples.r: EH-lah DEE-see kee EE-ah sheh-GAHR TAHR-jee, mahs sheh-GOH SEH-doo.
examples.en: She said she would arrive late, but she arrived early.

examples.t: Ele falou que tinha visto o relatório.
examples.r: EH-lee fah-LOH kee TEE-nyah VEES-too oo heh-lah-TOH-ree-oo.
examples.en: He said he had seen the report.

examples.t: Ela perguntou se dava tempo de entregar hoje.
examples.r: EH-lah pehr-goon-TOH see DAH-vah TEH(n)-poo jee en-treh-GAHR OH-jee.
examples.en: She asked whether there was time to deliver today.

mistakes.wrong: Ela disse que vai chegar ontem.
mistakes.right: Ela disse que ia chegar ontem.
mistakes.why: A past report moves the tense back: vai becomes ia.

mistakes.wrong: Ele falou que eu tinha visto o relatório.
mistakes.right: Ele falou que ele tinha visto o relatório.
mistakes.why: Keep the reported subject in the third person.

Say aloud: Gostaria de viajar para a Espanha.

culture.text: Brazil is one language with many accents, and the differences are regional before they are national: the carioca carioca r sounds like an h, the paulistano r is rolled, the nordestino opens the e and the o and speaks with a tighter rhythm, and the gaúcho of the South says tu where Rio de Janeiro says você. The sertão of the Northeast has its own vocabulary of drought and faith (a seca, o retirante, o cordel), and the Amazon has words that came from Tupi and now belong to everyone (tapioca, jacaré, maracujá). None of these is more Portuguese than another.

reading.text: Naquela quinta-feira eu cheguei a Salvador com uma mala pequena e muita vontade de andar. Chovia forte quando o ônibus parou, e as ruas do Pelourinho estavam cheias de gente correndo com guarda-chuva. Eu tinha reservado uma pousada perto do elevador, mas não sabia ler o mapa, então perguntei a um senhor que vendia acarajé na esquina. Ele riu, apontou para cima e disse que era só seguir a ladeira. Enquanto eu subia, um grupo começou a cantar dentro de um bar, e eu parei para ouvir antes de procurar o endereço.
reading.gloss: That Thursday I arrived in Salvador with a small suitcase and a strong wish to walk around. It was raining hard when the bus stopped, and the streets of Pelourinho were full of people running with umbrellas. I had booked a guesthouse near the elevator, but I could not read the map, so I asked a man selling acarajé on the corner. He laughed, pointed upwards and said I just had to go up the hill. While I was climbing, a group started singing inside a bar, and I stopped to listen before looking for the address.

listening.script: Você já foi ao Nordeste? — Já, fui duas vezes, mas só conheço o litoral. — Eu quero ir no ano que vem, em julho. Dizem que as festas juninas são impressionantes. — São mesmo. Se você puder, fique até o São João; vale a pena.
listening.gloss: Have you ever been to the Northeast? — Yes, twice, but I only know the coast. — I want to go next year, in July. They say the June festivals are impressive. — They really are. If you can, stay for Saint John's Day; it is worth it.

mistakes.why: A finished time (ontem) takes the simple past, not the compound perfect.

mistakes.wrong: Se eu ter dinheiro, eu viajo.
mistakes.right: Se eu tiver dinheiro, eu viajo.
mistakes.why: A real condition takes the future subjunctive: tiver.

mistakes.wrong: Fazem dois anos que eu moro aqui.
mistakes.right: Faz dois anos que eu moro aqui.
mistakes.why: Fazer for elapsed time is impersonal and stays singular.

task.title: Uma história em duas páginas de caderno
task.instructions: Write 120 to 150 words about a trip or a move: set the scene with the imperfeito (chovia, eu tinha, as ruas estavam), then give the events in the pretérito (cheguei, perguntei, ele riu). Use at least four linkers (quando, enquanto, então, depois, no fim). Then read it aloud and mark every verb; if a verb surprises you, check it against the lesson's model.
